addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

Spring Boot backend for the Tallyo sports dashboard. It ingests ESPN scoreboard/summary data, normalizes it into PostgreSQL, and serves a paginated game API consumed by the Tallyo frontend (Vercel). There is a sibling frontend repo at `../tallyo` that generates TypeScript types from `openapi.yaml`.

## Commands

```bash
./mvnw -q -DskipTests compile   # compile only
./mvnw test                     # run tests (there are currently none under src/test)
./mvnw spring-boot:run           # run locally, requires env vars below
./mvnw clean package             # build jar for deployment
./deploy.sh                      # build + docker compose down/up + tail logs (used in prod, requires .env)
```

Required env vars for local run: `API_KEY`, `SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME` (password defaults to empty, URL defaults to `jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/postgres`).

Runs on `http://localhost:8080`. Every API request needs header `x-api-key: <API_KEY>`.

## Architecture

Package root: `com.tallyo.tallyo_backend`. Flow for a request: `controller` → `service` (business logic, calls `EspnService` for live data or `GameRepository` for stored data) → `mapper` converts between ESPN `model` objects, JPA `entity` objects, and response `dto` objects.

- `model/espn/scoreboard`, `model/espn/box_score` — hand-written POJOs mirroring ESPN's JSON responses (scoreboard = schedule/scores/odds, box_score = per-game stats fetched from the `summary` endpoint). These are intentionally separate from `entity`.
- `mapper/EspnGameMapper`, `mapper/EspnBoxScoreMapper` — ESPN model → `Game`/`GameStat` entities.
- `mapper/GameResponseMapper` — entity → `GameResponse` DTO. Controllers must return DTOs, never JPA entities directly.
- `service/EspnService` — builds ESPN URLs (`{base}/{sport}/{league}/scoreboard` and `.../summary?event={id}`) and fetches via `RestTemplate`. League/sport path segments come from the `League` enum.
- `service/GameServiceImpl` — persists fetched games and runs a `@Scheduled(fixedRate = 20000)` job (`updateGamesForToday`) that checks `GameRepository.shouldUpdate()` (any game live or due to start in the last 24h) before re-fetching ESPN data for every league.
- `service/CalendarServiceImpl` — computes "current" league context (year/seasonType/week/date) via a native query (`GameRepository.findCurrentContext`) that prioritizes in-progress games, then next upcoming, then most recent final. Result is cached in `currentContext` (key = league + timezone), evicted every 5 minutes (`CacheConfig`).
- `enums/League` — single source of truth for supported leagues (`nfl`, `college-football`, `nhl`, `usa.1`) and their capability flags (`supportsYearFilter`, `supportsWeekFilter`, `supportsStandings`, `contextMode` — `"season"` vs `"date"` — `statsProfile`, `teamOrder`, `supportsOdds`, `supportsLiveDetails`). Controllers and services branch on these flags instead of hardcoding per-league logic.
- `config/ApiKeyAuthFilter` + `config/SecurityConfig` — stateless `x-api-key` header check via a filter placed before Spring Security's auth filter; CORS is locked to `https://tallyo.us` (update `SecurityConfig` if the frontend origin changes).
- `exception/GlobalExceptionHandler` — all errors return the same `ApiError` envelope (`code`, `message`, `details?`, `path?`, `timestamp?`). `InvalidRequestException` → 400; `DateTimeException` → 400 `INVALID_TIMEZONE`; `RestClientException`/`ResourceAccessException` (ESPN upstream failures) → 502; everything else → 500.

### Timezone/date handling

Endpoints computing "current" context or date boundaries accept a `userTimeZone` param (default `America/New_York`). Never hardcode a timezone for returned date context. The current-context cache key includes both league and timezone, so different timezones don't collide.

### Adding a new league

1. Add an enum entry in `League` with correct sport/value/capability flags.
2. Confirm the ESPN scoreboard/summary URLs resolve for that league's sport/value.
3. Confirm `EspnGameMapper`/`EspnBoxScoreMapper` handle its sport-specific fields safely.
4. Confirm `/context`, `/dates`, `/games/current` produce sane data (contextMode `"season"` vs `"date"` matters here).
5. Update `openapi.yaml` if request/response shape changes, then regenerate frontend types in `../tallyo`.

## API contract discipline

`openapi.yaml` is maintained by hand and is the source of truth consumed by the frontend's generated types. Any change to endpoint behavior, params, or response shape must update `openapi.yaml` in the same change. CI (`openapi-check.yml`) validates the YAML parses and that the project compiles, but does not diff the contract against the code — keeping them in sync is manual.

## Deployment

Push to `main` triggers `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, which SSHes into the prod host (via `cloudflared` tunnel) and runs `git pull && ./deploy.sh`, which rebuilds the jar and recreates the `docker-compose.yml` stack (`app` + `postgres` + `dozzle` log viewer). Hibernate runs with `ddl-auto: update` — schema changes apply automatically on boot, so be deliberate about entity changes.

# Tallyo Frontend ↔ Backend Integration

How this repo (`tallyo`, Next.js UI on Vercel) integrates with the sibling repo
`../tallyo-backend` (Spring Boot + PostgreSQL, deployed via docker-compose behind
`https://api.tallyo.us`).

## Big picture

```
Browser (SWR hooks in components)
   │  same-origin calls to /api/*
   ▼
Next.js API routes (src/app/api/*)          ← thin proxy layer, no business logic
   │  fetch ${BACKEND_URL}/api/v1/*  with header  x-api-key: ${API_KEY}
   ▼
Spring Boot backend (tallyo-backend)
   │  controller → service → mapper → dto
   ├─ PostgreSQL (games persisted from ESPN, refreshed by a 20s scheduled job)
   └─ ESPN APIs (scoreboard + summary ingestion)

Exception: standings and per-game stats bypass the backend entirely —
the Next routes call ESPN directly via src/lib/espn/espnService.ts.
```

The frontend has no database and no domain logic of its own; the backend is the
source of truth for game data, league capabilities, and the API contract.

## Route mapping

| Frontend route (Next) | Backend endpoint | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/games` | `GET /api/v1/games` | Forwards `league`, `year`, `seasonType`, `week`, `date`; unwraps the `PageResponse` and returns `body.content` |
| `GET /api/games/current` | `GET /api/v1/games/current` | Backend resolves "current" year/seasonType/week/date itself via `CalendarService` |
| `GET /api/context` | `GET /api/v1/games/context` or `/api/v1/games/dates` | Frontend `mode=season` → `/context` (returns `CurrentContext`); `mode=date` → `/dates` (returns available game dates) |
| `GET /api/leagues` | `GET /api/v1/leagues` | Returns `LeagueMetadata[]` derived from the backend `League` enum |

legacy `GET /api/v1/games/nhl-dates`; the frontend does not call either.

  it server-side from the `API_KEY` env var, so the key never reaches the browser.
- Backend side: `ApiKeyAuthFilter` (registered in `SecurityConfig`) compares the
  header to `${api.key}` and returns a `403` `ApiError` envelope on mismatch.

  the browser never talks to the backend directly (all calls are same-origin to
  the Next routes), so CORS only matters if that changes.

  and `API_KEY`. Both are server-only (not `NEXT_PUBLIC_`).

  backend repo; version 1.1.0, servers `https://api.tallyo.us` and `localhost:8080`).

  against the sibling repo's spec and writes `src/types/api.generated.ts`
  (never hand-edited).

  schemas as `GameResponse`, `CurrentContextResponse`, `LeagueMetadataResponse`,
  `ApiError`, etc.
- **CI enforcement:**
  - Frontend: `.github/workflows/contract-check.yml` runs `npm run check:api-contract`
    (regenerates types and fails on diff), so the checked-in types must match the spec.
  - Backend: `openapi-check.yml` validates the YAML parses and the project compiles,
    but does **not** diff the contract against the Java code — spec↔code sync is manual
    on the backend side.

  then run `npm run gen:api-types` here and commit the regenerated types.

## League capability sync

Both repos avoid per-league `if` branching by driving behavior off capability flags,
and the flags flow backend → frontend at runtime:

- Backend `enums/League` is the origin: `NFL`, `CFB`, `NHL`, `MLS` with flags
  (`supportsYearFilter`, `supportsWeekFilter`, `supportsStandings`,

  directly, not the backend).

1. Components resolve the browser timezone: `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`.

3. Next routes forward it to the backend as `userTimeZone=...` (URL-encoded).

A single `ApiError` envelope is shared end to end:
`{ code, message, details?, path?, timestamp? }`.

- Backend `GlobalExceptionHandler` maps everything to this shape
  (400 for invalid requests/timezones, 403 from the API-key filter,
  502 for ESPN upstream failures, 500 otherwise).

  return the backend's raw body and status untouched (see

  and `details` attached from the envelope, so components handle backend and
  ESPN-direct failures uniformly.

Freshness is a cooperation between backend ingestion and frontend polling:

- **Backend:** `GameServiceImpl.updateGamesForToday` runs `@Scheduled(fixedRate = 20000)`
  (every 20s) and re-fetches ESPN scoreboard data for all leagues, but only when
  `GameRepository.shouldUpdate()` says a game is live or recently started.
  `CalendarServiceImpl`'s current-context result is cached per league+timezone and
  evicted every 5 minutes.

frontend interval (10s).

  viewer). Hibernate runs `ddl-auto: update`, so entity changes migrate the
  schema automatically on boot.
- The two deploys are independent — the OpenAPI contract (plus the frontend's
  `DEFAULT_LEAGUE_METADATA` fallbacks) is what keeps them compatible across skew.

1. **Backend:** add the `League` enum entry (sport, ESPN path value, capability
   flags); verify ESPN scoreboard/summary URLs resolve and the mappers handle the
   sport's fields; confirm `/games`, `/games/current`, `/context`, `/dates` behave.

   query-param enums list the league ids).

   `statDisplayMaps.ts` if it's a new stats profile. The dynamic `[league]` route
   picks it up with no new routing.

The short version of how they integrate:

- **Proxy pattern with a twist.** Browser components use SWR against same-origin Next routes (`/api/games`, `/api/games/current`, `/api/context`, `/api/leagues`), which are thin pass-throughs to the Spring backend at `${BACKEND_URL}/api/v1/*`, attaching the `x-api-key` header server-side. Spring Boot 3 / Java, PostgreSQL (Hibernate `ddl-auto: update`), `RestTemplate`-based ESPN ingestion. All endpoints under `/api/v1`, guarded by an `x-api-key` header filter. Package root: `com.tallyo.tallyo_backend`.

## 1. Existing game-stats support

**Ingestion path exists and works, but is coarse.**

- **`entity/GameStat.java`** — composite-key row keyed by `GameStatKey{gameId, teamId, statType}` (`entity/GameStatKey.java`), plus a single `statValue` String. Table `game_stats`, unique constraint on `(game_id, stat_type, team_id)`. `@ManyToOne` back to `Game` via `game_id`.
- **`entity/Game.java`** (lines 43–46, 74–101) — holds `Map<GameStatKey, GameStat> stats` (`@OneToMany`, `EAGER`, `orphanRemoval`, `@JsonIgnore`). `addStats()` merges; `getStatsForJson()` (`@JsonProperty("stats")`) pivots the flat map into `StatResponse{homeStats, awayStats}` by comparing each stat's `teamId` to the home team's id (everything not home → away).
- **`model/espn/box_score/`** — POJOs for ESPN's `summary` endpoint, but only a thin slice: `EspnBoxscoreResponse{boxscore}` → `Boxscore{List<Team> teams}` → `Team{TeamDetail team, List<Statistic> statistics, homeAway}` → `Statistic{name, displayValue, value, label}`, `TeamDetail{id}`. `@JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true)`, so **everything else in the summary payload (scoring plays, leaders, win probability, drives, situation, format, etc.) is silently dropped.**
- **`mapper/EspnBoxScoreMapper.java`** — for each team, one `GameStat` per `Statistic`, storing `stat.getName()` → `stat.getDisplayValue()`. So the backend ingests **team-level box-score totals only** (e.g. `totalYards`, `firstDowns`, `possessionTime` for football; whatever the summary's `boxscore.teams[].statistics` array contains per sport). No player-level stats, no numeric typing (all Strings).

**Is it exposed in the API today?** Yes. `GameResponseMapper.toResponse()` (line 43) calls `game.getStatsForJson()` and sets `.stats(...)`. `GameResponse.stats` is a `StatResponse` with `homeStats`/`awayStats` maps (`dto/GameResponse.java:37`, `dto/StatResponse.java`). openapi.yaml models this as `TeamStats` (lines 63–73, referenced at 136–137). So the `homeStats`/`awayStats` maps **are already part of every game in the `/api/v1/games*` responses.**

**What triggers stats fetching:**
- `EspnService.fetchStatsForGame(gameId, league)` builds `.../summary?event={id}` and maps to `GameStat`s (`service/EspnService.java:99–125`).
- Gated by a `shouldFetchStats` boolean threaded through `fetchGames(...)` → `attachStatsToGame` (lines 39–97). When true, it makes **one summary call per game** (N+1 against ESPN).
- **POST `/api/v1/games`** exposes `shouldFetchStats` (default `false`) — `GameController.updateGames` → `GameServiceImpl.updateGames`.
- **The 20s scheduled job DOES fetch stats:** `GameServiceImpl.updateGamesForToday()` (`@Scheduled(fixedRate=20000)`) calls `espnService.fetchGames(league, yesterday, today, true)` with `shouldFetchStats=true` for **every** league (lines 57–85), but only after `gameRepository.shouldUpdate()` returns true. So for any window where a game is live or recently scheduled, stored stats refresh every ~20s. Because ingestion is date-windowed (yesterday+today) and per-game, live games get near-real-time team box-score updates already.

## 2. Scoring plays

**Not ingested, not stored, not served — completely absent.** No entity, no POJO field, no mapper, no DTO. Grep for `scoringPlay`/`scoring_play` returns nothing. ESPN's summary endpoint (already called for stats) contains a `scoringPlays` array, but `EspnBoxscoreResponse` only declares `boxscore` and drops the rest via `ignoreUnknown`. This is entirely greenfield backend work.

## 3. Standings

**No standings support of any kind server-side.** No standings entity, no repository query, no controller endpoint, no ESPN standings fetch (ESPN standings live at a different host/path, e.g. `.../v2/sports/{sport}/{league}/standings`, which is never constructed anywhere). The `Team` entity (`entity/Team.java`) *has* standings-shaped columns (`wins`, `losses`, `ties`, `conference`, `division`, `homeRecord`, `roadRecord`, `recordVsConference`, `recordVsDivision`, `pointsFor`, `pointsAgainst`, `pointDifferential`, `streak`, `winPercent`, `seed`, `ranking`) — **but `EspnGameMapper.toTeam()` only populates `name/abbreviation/logo/colors/location/record/homeRecord/roadRecord/score`** (lines 187–207). The rest are never written and stay null.

**`League.supportsStandings`** flag: NFL/CFB `true`, NHL/MLS `false`. It is only surfaced to the client via `LeagueMetadataResponse.fromLeague()` (`GET /api/v1/leagues`) and echoed in openapi.yaml. **Nothing on the server branches on it** — no code path reads `isSupportsStandings()` to decide behavior. It is purely a client-facing capability hint today.

## 4. EspnService & RestTemplate

`service/EspnService.java`:
- **Scoreboard URL (date range):** `{baseUrl}/{sport}/{league}/scoreboard?limit={limit}&dates={start}-{end}` where dates are `yyyyMMdd` (line 40).
- **Scoreboard URL (year):** `...scoreboard?limit={limit}&dates={year}0101-{year}1231` (line 77); year 0 → current year.
- **Summary URL:** `{baseUrl}/{sport}/{league}/summary?event={gameId}` (line 101).
- `sport`/`league` path segments come from `League.getSport().getValue()` and `League.getValue()` (`college-football`, `usa.1`, etc.).
- **Parsing:** scoreboard → `EspnScoreboardResponse` → `events[]` → `EspnGameMapper.toGame` (rich mapper, `model/espn/scoreboard/*` ~40 POJOs incl. odds, situation, records, venue, status). Summary → `EspnBoxscoreResponse` (thin, boxscore only).
- **Error handling:** scoreboard fetch logs + **rethrows** (`fetchGamesForUrl`, lines 127–134) so failures propagate to `GlobalExceptionHandler` → 502. Summary/stats fetch **swallows** exceptions (logs, returns empty list — lines 119–121, and `attachStatsToGame` catches per game lines 62–73), so stats are best-effort and never fail a request.

**`config/EspnApiProperties.java`** — `@ConfigurationProperties("espn.api")`: only `baseUrl` and nested `scoreboard.limit`. Values in `application.yml`: `base-url: https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports`, `scoreboard.limit: 1000`. No standings/summary-specific config.

**`config/RestTemplateConfig.java`** — bare `new RestTemplate()`. **No connect/read timeouts, no retry, no error handler, no connection pooling.** A hung ESPN call can block a scheduler thread indefinitely — a real concern if you add per-game summary fan-out for standings/scoring plays.

## 5. Caching & scheduling

- **`config/CacheConfig.java`** — `ConcurrentMapCacheManager` with a single cache: **`currentContext`**. No TTL support (in-memory map); manually evicted wholesale every 5 min by `@Scheduled(fixedRate=300000) @CacheEvict(allEntries=true)`. Only `CalendarServiceImpl.getCurrentContext` is `@Cacheable` (key `league + ':' + timezone`). **Game data and stats are NOT cached** — they're read from Postgres each request.
- **Scheduled jobs (only two):**
  1. `GameServiceImpl.updateGamesForToday` — every 20s; guarded by `GameRepository.shouldUpdate()`; fetches all leagues (yesterday→today) **with stats**.
  2. `CacheConfig.evictCurrentContextCache` — every 5 min.
- **`GameRepository.shouldUpdate()`** (native, lines 68–76) — returns true iff there exists a game within the last 24h that is live (`STATUS_IN_PROGRESS`/`HALFTIME`/`END_PERIOD`) **or** scheduled with a start time already passed. This is the throttle that stops ESPN polling when nothing is happening.
- **`config/LeagueConstraintSync.java`** — `@PostConstruct` runs raw DDL via `JdbcTemplate` to drop+recreate CHECK constraints `teams_league_check` and `games_league_check` so the `league` column only accepts current `League.values()`. Keeps DB enum constraints in sync with the Java enum on every boot; failures are logged, not fatal. **Note:** any new standings/scoring-plays table referencing `league` would need the same treatment (or reuse the team/game FK).

## 6. API surface & DTOs

**Endpoints:**
- `GameController` (`/api/v1/games`):
  - `GET /` — params `league` (req), `year`, `seasonType`, `week`, `size`(100), `page`(0), `date`, `sortBy`(id), `userTimeZone`(America/New_York) → `PageResponse<GameResponse>`.
  - `GET /current` — `league`(req), optional `year`/`seasonType`/`week`, `userTimeZone`, `size`, `page`, `sortBy`; resolves current context then delegates → `PageResponse<GameResponse>`.
  - `GET /context` — `league`, `userTimeZone` → `CurrentContext`.
  - `GET /dates` — `league`, `userTimeZone` → `List<String>`.
  - `GET /nhl-dates` — `userTimeZone` → `List<String>` (hardcoded NHL; **not in openapi.yaml**).
  - `POST /` — `league`, `year`, `shouldFetchStats` → `UpdateResponse{gameCount, durationMs}` (**not in openapi.yaml**).
- `LeagueController` (`/api/v1/leagues`): `GET /` → `List<LeagueMetadataResponse>`.

**DTO shapes:**
- `GameResponse` — ~35 fields incl. nested `homeTeam`/`awayTeam` (`TeamResponse`), `gameOdd` (`GameOddResponse{spreadText}`), `stats` (`StatResponse{homeStats, awayStats}`), plus live fields (`period`, `lastPlay`, `currentDownAndDistance`, `possessionTeamId`, timeouts, win percentages) and `finalGame`/`final` duplication.
- `CurrentContext{year, seasonType, date, week}`.
- `PageResponse<T>{content, page, size, totalElements, totalPages, first, last}`.
- `LeagueMetadataResponse{id, label, path, supportsStandings, contextMode, supportsYearFilter, supportsWeekFilter, statsProfile, teamOrder, supportsOdds, supportsLiveDetails, showInHeader, showInDashboard}` (`showInHeader`/`showInDashboard` hardcoded `true`).
- `UpdateResponse{gameCount, durationMs}` (record).
- `ApiError{code, message, details, path, timestamp}`.

**`GlobalExceptionHandler` mapping:** `InvalidRequestException` → 400 `BAD_REQUEST`; `DateTimeException` → 400 `INVALID_TIMEZONE`; `ResourceAccessException`/`RestClientException` → 502 `UPSTREAM_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`; catch-all `Exception` → 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR`. - **Missing endpoints:** `POST /api/v1/games` and `GET /api/v1/games/nhl-dates` are not documented.

- No `error` responses documented for `/leagues` beyond 403; overall the spec lags the code.

## 7. Persistence

- **Entities:** `Game` (`games`), `Team` (`teams`, composite key `TeamKey{teamId, league}`), `GameOdd` (`game_odds`, one-to-one), `GameStat` (`game_stats`, composite `GameStatKey`), plus embeddables `TeamKey`/`GameStatKey`. **No standings or scoring-play entities.**

---

## What NEW backend work is required

### (a) League standings — greenfield, ~all new
1. **ESPN client:** add a standings fetch in `EspnService` — ESPN standings are on a *different* host/path family than the site scoreboard API (e.g. `https://site.web.api.espn.com/.../standings` or `.../v2/sports/{sport}/{league}/standings`), so `EspnApiProperties.baseUrl` won't suffice; add a second base URL + new URL builder.
2. **POJOs:** new `model/espn/standings/*` tree (ESPN standings JSON is deeply nested: children/groups → standings.entries → team + stats[]). None exist.
3. **Persistence:** either enrich the existing `Team` columns (which already exist but are unpopulated — cheapest path, populate wins/losses/conference/division/etc. and store as a standings snapshot) or add a dedicated `Standings`/`StandingRow` entity keyed by `(league, season, teamId)`. If a new table references `league`, extend `LeagueConstraintSync`.
4. **Mapper + DTO + endpoint:** `EspnStandingsMapper`, a `StandingsResponse` DTO (grouped by conference/division), and e.g. `GET /api/v1/standings?league=&season=` in a new or existing controller. Branch on `League.supportsStandings` (currently unused server-side) to 400/empty for NHL/MLS.
5. **Scheduling/caching:** standings change slowly — add a separate low-frequency scheduled refresh and/or a `standings` cache in `CacheConfig` rather than reusing the 20s live loop.
6. **openapi.yaml:** add schemas + path.

### (b) Per-game stats + scoring plays for live games
- **Stats:** foundation already exists end-to-end (ingest → store → `homeStats`/`awayStats` in `GameResponse`, refreshed every 20s for live games). Gaps to close only if the frontend needs *more* than team totals: the summary payload's player-level stats, leaders, and typed/numeric values are currently discarded by the thin `box_score` POJOs and the `statType→String` model. Expanding requires new box_score POJO fields, a richer `GameStat` (or new player-stat entity), and mapper/DTO changes.
- **Scoring plays:** fully greenfield:
  1. Extend `EspnBoxscoreResponse` (or a new `model/espn/summary/*` tree) to deserialize the summary's `scoringPlays` array (it's already fetched in the same call, just dropped).
  2. New `ScoringPlay` entity/table keyed by game (+ sequence) — or persist as JSON on `Game`.
  3. New mapper + a `ScoringPlaysResponse`/nested field on `GameResponse`.
  4. Wire into the same `shouldFetchStats`/20s live loop so live games stay current; consider that this is already an N+1 summary call per game — combining scoring-plays parsing into the existing summary fetch avoids extra ESPN round-trips.
  5. openapi.yaml additions.

### Cross-cutting risks to flag
- **`RestTemplate` has no timeouts** (`RestTemplateConfig`) — adding more per-game/standings fan-out amplifies the risk of the 20s scheduler thread hanging on a slow ESPN response. Add connect/read timeouts before scaling ESPN calls.
- **Summary fetch is per-game (N+1)** and its exceptions are swallowed — fine for best-effort stats, but scoring plays feeding a live UI may want stricter freshness/error signaling.
- **CORS is locked to `https://tallyo.us`** (`SecurityConfig`) — if the browser starts hitting these new endpoints directly (the stated goal), confirm the frontend origin(s) are covered.
- **openapi.yaml already drifts** from the code; new endpoints must be added by hand (CI won't catch omissions) so the frontend's generated types stay correct.

  - `GET /` — params `league` (req), `year`, `seasonType`, `week`, `size`(100), `page`(0), `date`, `sortBy`(id), `userTimeZone`(America/New_York) → `PageResponse<GameResponse>`.
  - `GET /current` — `league`(req), optional `year`/`seasonType`/`week`, `userTimeZone`, `size`, `page`, `sortBy`; resolves current context then delegates → `PageResponse<GameResponse>`.
  - `GET /context` — `league`, `userTimeZone` → `CurrentContext`.
  - `GET /dates` — `league`, `userTimeZone` → `List<String>`.
  - `GET /nhl-dates` — `userTimeZone` → `List<String>` (hardcoded NHL; **not in openapi.yaml**).
  - `POST /` — `league`, `year`, `shouldFetchStats` → `UpdateResponse{gameCount, durationMs}` (**not in openapi.yaml**).
- `LeagueController` (`/api/v1/leagues`): `GET /` → `List<LeagueMetadataResponse>`.

**DTO shapes:**
- `GameResponse` — ~35 fields incl. nested `homeTeam`/`awayTeam` (`TeamResponse`), `gameOdd` (`GameOddResponse{spreadText}`), `stats` (`StatResponse{homeStats, awayStats}`), plus live fields (`period`, `lastPlay`, `currentDownAndDistance`, `possessionTeamId`, timeouts, win percentages) and `finalGame`/`final` duplication.
- `CurrentContext{year, seasonType, date, week}`.
- `PageResponse<T>{content, page, size, totalElements, totalPages, first, last}`.
- `LeagueMetadataResponse{id, label, path, supportsStandings, contextMode, supportsYearFilter, supportsWeekFilter, statsProfile, teamOrder, supportsOdds, supportsLiveDetails, showInHeader, showInDashboard}` (`showInHeader`/`showInDashboard` hardcoded `true`).
- `UpdateResponse{gameCount, durationMs}` (record).
- `ApiError{code, message, details, path, timestamp}`.

**`GlobalExceptionHandler` mapping:** `InvalidRequestException` → 400 `BAD_REQUEST`; `DateTimeException` → 400 `INVALID_TIMEZONE`; `ResourceAccessException`/`RestClientException` → 502 `UPSTREAM_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`; catch-all `Exception` → 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR`. All wrap into `ApiError` with request path + timestamp.

**openapi.yaml drift (spec is hand-maintained; CI only checks it parses + compiles):**
- **Missing endpoints:** `POST /api/v1/games` and `GET /api/v1/games/nhl-dates` are not documented.
- **Missing params** on `GET /api/v1/games`: `size`, `page`, `sortBy` (documented set omits them); `GET /current` documents only `league`+`userTimeZone` but code accepts `year/seasonType/week/size/page/sortBy`.
- **`Team` schema** in spec lists ~11 fields; `TeamResponse`/entity expose ~25 (seed, ranking, wins, losses, ties, conference, division, homeRecord, roadRecord, recordVs*, pointsFor/Against, pointDifferential, streak, winPercent) — most currently null but present in JSON.
- No `error` responses documented for `/leagues` beyond 403; overall the spec lags the code.

## 7. Persistence

- **Entities:** `Game` (`games`), `Team` (`teams`, composite key `TeamKey{teamId, league}`), `GameOdd` (`game_odds`, one-to-one), `GameStat` (`game_stats`, composite `GameStatKey`), plus embeddables `TeamKey`/`GameStatKey`. **No standings or scoring-play entities.**
- **Repository:** single `GameRepository` (no `TeamRepository`, no `GameStatRepository` — stats persist via `Game` cascade). Key queries:
  - `getGames(...)` (JPQL) — dynamic filters + `ORDER BY` custom status priority (live → scheduled → final).
  - `findCurrentContext(league, now)` (native) — picks the single most relevant game (live > next upcoming > most recent final) and returns its `(year, seasonType, date, week)` projected into `CurrentContext`.
  - `shouldUpdate()` (native) — the scheduler throttle (§5).
  - `getGameDates(league)` (native) — distinct `iso_date`s.
- **Hibernate:** `ddl-auto: update` (schema auto-migrates on boot — new tables/columns apply automatically), `open-in-view: false`, `show-sql: false`. `Game.stats` is `FetchType.EAGER`, so every game load pulls its stats.

---

## What NEW backend work is required

### (a) League standings — greenfield, ~all new
1. **ESPN client:** add a standings fetch in `EspnService` — ESPN standings are on a *different* host/path family than the site scoreboard API (e.g. `https://site.web.api.espn.com/.../standings` or `.../v2/sports/{sport}/{league}/standings`), so `EspnApiProperties.baseUrl` won't suffice; add a second base URL + new URL builder.
2. **POJOs:** new `model/espn/standings/*` tree (ESPN standings JSON is deeply nested: children/groups → standings.entries → team + stats[]). None exist.
3. **Persistence:** either enrich the existing `Team` columns (which already exist but are unpopulated — cheapest path, populate wins/losses/conference/division/etc. and store as a standings snapshot) or add a dedicated `Standings`/`StandingRow` entity keyed by `(league, season, teamId)`. If a new table references `league`, extend `LeagueConstraintSync`.
4. **Mapper + DTO + endpoint:** `EspnStandingsMapper`, a `StandingsResponse` DTO (grouped by conference/division), and e.g. `GET /api/v1/standings?league=&season=` in a new or existing controller. Branch on `League.supportsStandings` (currently unused server-side) to 400/empty for NHL/MLS.
5. **Scheduling/caching:** standings change slowly — add a separate low-frequency scheduled refresh and/or a `standings` cache in `CacheConfig` rather than reusing the 20s live loop.
6. **openapi.yaml:** add schemas + path.

### (b) Per-game stats + scoring plays for live games
- **Stats:** foundation already exists end-to-end (ingest → store → `homeStats`/`awayStats` in `GameResponse`, refreshed every 20s for live games). Gaps to close only if the frontend needs *more* than team totals: the summary payload's player-level stats, leaders, and typed/numeric values are currently discarded by the thin `box_score` POJOs and the `statType→String` model. Expanding requires new box_score POJO fields, a richer `GameStat` (or new player-stat entity), and mapper/DTO changes.
- **Scoring plays:** fully greenfield:
  1. Extend `EspnBoxscoreResponse` (or a new `model/espn/summary/*` tree) to deserialize the summary's `scoringPlays` array (it's already fetched in the same call, just dropped).
  2. New `ScoringPlay` entity/table keyed by game (+ sequence) — or persist as JSON on `Game`.
  3. New mapper + a `ScoringPlaysResponse`/nested field on `GameResponse`.
  4. Wire into the same `shouldFetchStats`/20s live loop so live games stay current; consider that this is already an N+1 summary call per game — combining scoring-plays parsing into the existing summary fetch avoids extra ESPN round-trips.
  5. openapi.yaml additions.

### Cross-cutting risks to flag
- **`RestTemplate` has no timeouts** (`RestTemplateConfig`) — adding more per-game/standings fan-out amplifies the risk of the 20s scheduler thread hanging on a slow ESPN response. Add connect/read timeouts before scaling ESPN calls.
- **Summary fetch is per-game (N+1)** and its exceptions are swallowed — fine for best-effort stats, but scoring plays feeding a live UI may want stricter freshness/error signaling.
- **CORS is locked to `https://tallyo.us`** (`SecurityConfig`) — if the browser starts hitting these new endpoints directly (the stated goal), confirm the frontend origin(s) are covered.
- **openapi.yaml already drifts** from the code; new endpoints must be added by hand (CI won't catch omissions) so the frontend's generated types stay correct.

input.prompt:
Design an implementation plan for rebuilding the Tallyo frontend from scratch as a pure client of its Spring backend, plus the backend additions needed to make that possible. Two repos: /Users/jackpotter/projects/tallyo (Next.js 16 App Router, Tailwind 4, SWR, deployed on Vercel at tallyo.us) and /Users/jackpotter/projects/tallyo-backend (Spring Boot 3 + PostgreSQL, deployed via docker-compose at api.tallyo.us; push to main auto-deploys, so backend work must go on a branch).

## User decisions (fixed)
- Backend-only UI: standings and per-game stats/scoring-plays move from the frontend's ESPN-direct layer into the Spring backend. New UI talks ONLY to the backend (via Next API-route proxies that inject x-api-key from env; BACKEND_URL + API_KEY env vars).
- Stack: Next.js App Router again, fresh code on a new branch in tallyo, starting from scratch (keep tooling: Next 16, Tailwind 4, TS strict, eslint+prettier, the Ruby openapi type generator at scripts/generate-api-types.rb which reads ../tallyo-backend/openapi.yaml and writes src/types/api.generated.ts; CI check npm run check:api-contract).
- Full feature parity target: Header nav, root Dashboard (live games per league, 10s poll, isLiveDashboardGame filter incl. 6h recently-started window), /[league] pages (season/week/year selectors for nfl/cfb, date selector for nhl/mls, game grid), game cards (compact + expanded: scores, possession, timeouts NFL, live down/distance, last play, win probability, scoring plays, player stat leaders, team stats via per-profile display maps, spreadText odds for nfl/cfb, ESPN link, venue), standings tables (NFL/NHL/MLS/default profiles with section grouping — NHL divisions + wildcard tagging), maintenance mode middleware (src/proxy.ts, NEXT_PUBLIC_MAINTENANCE_MODE).

## Current state (from exploration)

### Backend has already
- Game ingestion: EspnService fetches scoreboard ({base}/{sport}/{league}/scoreboard?limit&dates=yyyyMMdd-yyyyMMdd, base=site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports) → EspnGameMapper → Game/Team/GameOdd entities. @Scheduled(fixedRate=20000) job in GameServiceImpl refreshes yesterday+today for all leagues WITH stats when GameRepository.shouldUpdate() (any live/recently-started game).
- Team box-score stats: summary endpoint ({base}/{sport}/{league}/summary?event={id}) → thin EspnBoxscoreResponse (ONLY boxscore.teams[].statistics; everything else dropped via ignoreUnknown) → GameStat entities (composite key gameId/teamId/statType, String value) → exposed on every GameResponse as stats.homeStats/awayStats maps. Already in openapi.yaml as TeamStats.
- Endpoints: GET /api/v1/games (league, year, seasonType, week, date, userTimeZone, paging), /games/current, /games/context, /games/dates, /games/nhl-dates (legacy, undocumented), POST /games (undocumented), GET /api/v1/leagues (LeagueMetadataResponse from League enum: id/label/path/supportsStandings/contextMode/supportsYearFilter/supportsWeekFilter/statsProfile/teamOrder/supportsOdds/supportsLiveDetails/showInHeader/showInDashboard — last two hardcoded true).
- League enum = capability source of truth: NFL(season,football), CFB(season,football), NHL(date,hockey), MLS(date,soccer,home-left). supportsStandings currently true only for NFL/CFB and unused server-side; frontend force-enables nhl/mls standings client-side today (should be fixed: set supportsStandings=true for NHL/MLS in the enum since backend will serve standings).
- Error envelope ApiError{code,message,details,path,timestamp} via GlobalExceptionHandler (400 BAD_REQUEST/INVALID_TIMEZONE, 502 UPSTREAM_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE for ESPN failures, 500 INTERNAL_ERROR); ApiKeyAuthFilter 403.
- CacheConfig: ConcurrentMapCacheManager, single 'currentContext' cache evicted every 5min. LeagueConstraintSync: @PostConstruct DDL sync of league CHECK constraints on games/teams tables. Hibernate ddl-auto:update. RestTemplateConfig: bare RestTemplate, NO timeouts (must fix before adding fan-out). Team entity already has unpopulated standings-shaped columns (wins/losses/conference/division/pointsFor/etc.) but I lean cache-only standings, no persistence.
- openapi.yaml (hand-maintained, v1.1.0) already drifts: missing POST /games, nhl-dates, paging params, ~14 Team fields. Plan should include reconciling it since frontend types are generated from it.

### What backend must ADD (greenfield)
1. Standings: ESPN standings live on different hosts than the scoreboard base (frontend today uses cdn.espn.com/core/{league}/standings?xhr=1 for nfl/cfb and site.api.espn.com/apis/v2/... + cdn fallbacks with retry-until-non-empty for nhl/mls). Need: new config for standings URLs per league (fallback list), model/espn/standings POJOs OR lenient JsonNode traversal (frontend's standingsMapper.ts walks arbitrary shapes: content.standings.groups | children | recursive groups/children/items → entries → stats[] type→displayValue dynamic map, synthesized record + differential, sort by seed; NHL section logic groups by division). Decide: replicate the dynamic Record<string,string> per-team stats map in the DTO (frontend Standings = { groupName, teams: Team[dynamic stat keys] }) vs a typed DTO. Serve via GET /api/v1/standings?league=, cached (e.g. @Cacheable 'standings' with ~15-60min scheduled evict), no DB table. 400 for leagues without supportsStandings.
2. Scoring plays + player stat leaders: extend the EXISTING summary fetch (same payload, currently dropped) — richer summary POJOs. Frontend shapes today: Stat{name,displayName,shortDisplayName,abbreviation,value,displayValue,playerName,playerShortName,teamId} keyed `${name}-${teamId}` from leaders; ScoringPlay{id,teamId,teamName(abbrev),displayText,homeScore,awayScore,scoringType(abbrev),quarter(period.number),clock}. Per-league summary payload quirks (nfl/cfb: gamepackageJSON.leaders/scoringPlays via cdn.espn.com/core/{league}/game?xhr=1&gameId=; nhl: payload.leaders + onIce scoring plays; mls: arrays) — BUT note backend uses site.api.espn.com summary endpoint which has a different (cleaner) shape than the cdn.espn.com xhr payloads the frontend scrapes; prefer the site.api.espn.com summary shape (it contains leaders + scoringPlays top-level for football; verify per sport). Decide exposure: new GET /api/v1/games/{gameId}/details (leaders + scoringPlays, polled by expanded cards) vs embedding on GameResponse (payload bloat on list endpoints). Persist scoring plays (new entity, wire LeagueConstraintSync) vs serve from cache/live-fetch — weigh: the 20s job already does per-game summary N+1; persisting keeps /details DB-only and survives restarts; cache-only is simpler.
3. Hardening: RestTemplate timeouts (connect/read), openapi.yaml updated with all new + missing existing endpoints/schemas.

### Frontend rebuild notes
- New branch in tallyo (e.g. ui-v2). Fresh src/: delete ambient global types (game.ts/team.ts/etc. — they diverge from generated contract: required-vs-optional mismatches, index-signature Team), all of src/lib/espn, dead odds code. Everything types from api.generated.ts via api-contract.ts aliases.

I have a complete picture of both codebases. Here is the implementation plan.

---

# Tallyo Rebuild: Backend-Only Frontend + Backend Additions

## Architecture summary of decisions made

1. **Standings**: backend-served via `GET /api/v1/standings?league=`, cache-only (no DB), lenient `JsonNode` traversal port of the frontend's `standingsMapper.ts`, config-driven fallback URL lists. DTO uses **typed identity fields + one dynamic `stats` map** (not a fully-dynamic team object) — cleanest expressible shape in OpenAPI, and the Ruby generator already supports `additionalProperties`.
2. **Game details (leaders + scoring plays)**: **persisted** in two new entities populated by the *existing* 20s summary fetch (zero extra ESPN calls), served by a new **`GET /api/v1/games/{gameId}/details`** endpoint (no `league` param needed — `games.id` is already the sole PK, so ESPN event ids are globally unique in this system). Not embedded on `GameResponse` (list-payload bloat; expanded cards poll details independently at 10s, exactly like today's `/api/stats` flow).
3. **New tables carry no `league` column** (keyed by gameId), so `LeagueConstraintSync` needs no changes.
4. **League enum flips**: `supportsStandings=true` and `supportsLiveDetails=true` for NHL and MLS. Both are backward-safe for the old UI (it force-enables nhl/mls standings client-side anyway, and its ESPN-direct `/api/stats` route already supports nhl/mls).
5. **Frontend**: fresh `src/` on branch `ui-v2`, everything typed from `api.generated.ts`, one shared backend-proxy helper for all API routes, one typed client module for URL building. Presentation-only maps (statDisplayMaps, UI_PRESETS, standings column profiles, NHL wildcard logic) stay client-side keyed by `statsProfile`/league id.
6. **Games proxy keeps unwrapping `PageResponse.content` to a plain array** (paging is unused at size=100; keeps components simple and matches today's behavior).

---

## Phase 1 — Backend: branch + hardening (tallyo-backend, branch `feature/ui-v2-api` off `main`)

**Files to modify:**
- `src/main/java/com/tallyo/tallyo_backend/config/RestTemplateConfig.java` — build via `RestTemplateBuilder` with `connectTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(5))`, `readTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10))`. Do this first; standings adds fan-out to cdn.espn.com.
- `src/main/java/com/tallyo/tallyo_backend/enums/League.java` — NHL: `supportsStandings=true, supportsLiveDetails=true`; MLS: same. (NFL/CFB unchanged.)
- `src/main/java/com/tallyo/tallyo_backend/config/CacheConfig.java` — `ConcurrentMapCacheManager("currentContext", "standings")`; add `@Scheduled(fixedRate = 1_800_000) @CacheEvict(value = "standings", allEntries = true)` (30 min — standings change only after games end; the existing 5-min context evict stays).

Validate: `./mvnw compile` and boot against local postgres; confirm `/api/v1/leagues` now reports the flipped flags.

## Phase 2 — Backend: standings

**New files:**
- `config/EspnStandingsProperties.java` — `@ConfigurationProperties(prefix = "espn.standings")` holding `Map<String, List<String>> urls` (league id → ordered fallback URL list). Populate `application.yml` with exactly the URLs from the frontend's `espnEndpoints.ts`: nfl/cfb single cdn.espn.com `core/{league}/standings?xhr=1` URL; nhl the 7-URL fallback chain; mls the 2-URL chain.
- `mapper/EspnStandingsMapper.java` — direct port of `src/lib/espn/mappers/standingsMapper.ts` using Jackson `JsonNode`: `content.standings.groups` → `children` filter → recursive walk over `groups|children|items` collecting groups with entries; per group recurse for entries carrying division name; per entry build team from `entry.team` (id/displayName/abbreviation/logos[0].href/location/seed) + dynamic `stats[]` `type → displayValue` map; synthesize `record` (`wins-losses-ties`) and `differential` (pointsfor − pointsagainst) when absent; sort teams by numeric seed.
- `service/StandingsService.java` + `service/StandingsServiceImpl.java` — `@Cacheable(value = "standings", key = "#league.name()")`; iterate fallback URLs, `restTemplate.getForObject(url, JsonNode.class)`, map, return first non-empty result; if all URLs fail/empty throw the existing upstream exception → 502 `UPSTREAM_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. Throw `InvalidRequestException` (400) when `!league.isSupportsStandings()`.
- `dto/StandingsTeamResponse.java` and `dto/StandingsGroupResponse.java`:

```
StandingsGroup { groupName: String, teams: List<StandingsTeam> }
StandingsTeam  { id, name, abbreviation, logo, location,
                 seed?, conference?, division?, record?, differential?,
                 stats: Map<String,String> }   // dynamic type→displayValue (points, gamesplayed, winpercent, vsconf, vsdiv, pointsfor, pointsagainst, streak, lasttengames, playoffseed, total, ...)
```

- `controller/StandingsController.java` — `GET /api/v1/standings?league=` → `List<StandingsGroupResponse>`, reusing the `League.valueOf` pattern from `GameController`.

Validate with curl for all four leagues (NHL must produce division names on teams; CFB must produce multiple conference groups).

## Phase 3 — Backend: leaders + scoring plays

**New entities** (populated by the same summary payload the 20s job already fetches):
- `entity/ScoringPlay.java` + `entity/ScoringPlayKey.java` — table `scoring_plays`, composite key `(gameId, playId)`; columns: teamId, teamAbbreviation, displayText, homeScore, awayScore, scoringType, period, clock, sequence (insertion order).
- `entity/GameLeader.java` + `entity/GameLeaderKey.java` — table `game_leaders`, composite key `(gameId, teamId, statName)` mirroring `GameStatKey`; columns: displayName, shortDisplayName, teamAbbreviation, value (Double), displayValue, playerName, playerShortName. Hibernate `ddl-auto: update` creates both tables; no `LeagueConstraintSync` change needed (no league column).

**Modified files:**
- `model/espn/box_score/EspnBoxscoreResponse.java` — add `private JsonNode leaders;` and `private JsonNode scoringPlays;` (keep the thin typed boxscore as-is; JsonNode absorbs per-sport shape drift).
- New `mapper/EspnSummaryDetailsMapper.java` — lenient extraction: football (`leaders[].leaders[].leaders[0].athlete`, `scoringPlays[]` with `team.id/abbreviation, text, homeScore, awayScore, scoringType.abbreviation, period.number, clock.displayValue`) matching the frontend's `statsMapper.ts` field-for-field; hockey/soccer branches per `league.getSport()` with null-safe fallbacks to empty lists. **Verify actual site.api.espn.com summary shapes per sport with curl during this phase** (see open questions).
- `service/EspnService.java` — in `attachStatsToGame` / `fetchStatsForGame`, parse the *single* summary response once into GameStats + GameLeaders + ScoringPlays; add `game.addLeaders(...)`, `game.addScoringPlays(...)` (cascade collections on `Game` like `addStats`).
- `entity/Game.java` — two new `@OneToMany(cascade = ALL, orphanRemoval = true)` collections + add helpers.
- New `dto/GameDetailsResponse.java`, `dto/StatLeaderResponse.java`, `dto/ScoringPlayResponse.java`:

```
GameDetails { gameId: string, leaders: StatLeader[], scoringPlays: ScoringPlay[] }
StatLeader  { name, displayName, shortDisplayName, abbreviation, value?: number,
              displayValue, playerName, playerShortName, teamId }
ScoringPlay { id, teamId, teamName, displayText, homeScore, awayScore,
              scoringType, period: number, clock }
```

- `controller/GameController.java` — `GET /api/v1/games/{gameId}/details`; 404 `GAME_NOT_FOUND` (add to `GlobalExceptionHandler` with a `ResourceNotFoundException`) if game id unknown; DB-only read, sorted scoringPlays by sequence.

## Phase 4 — Contract: openapi.yaml reconciliation + type regen

`openapi.yaml` (bump to 1.2.0, additions only — existing paths untouched):
- Add paths: `/api/v1/standings`, `/api/v1/games/{gameId}/details`, `POST /api/v1/games` (document as admin backfill), `/api/v1/games/nhl-dates` (marked `deprecated: true`).
- Add missing query params on `/games` + `/games/current`: `size`, `page`, `sortBy`.
- Add schemas: `StandingsGroup`, `StandingsTeam` (with `stats: additionalProperties: string`), `GameDetails`, `StatLeader`, `ScoringPlay`, `UpdateResponse`.
- Fix `Team` schema drift: add the ~14 real `TeamResponse`/entity fields (seed, ranking, wins, losses, ties, conference, division, home, road, vsconf, vsdiv, pointsfor, pointsagainst, differential, streak, winpercent) as optional strings, and loosen `required` to what the backend actually guarantees.

Then in tallyo (on `ui-v2`): `npm run gen:api-types`, commit `src/types/api.generated.ts`. CI `check:api-contract` keeps them locked.

## Phase 5 — Frontend rebuild (tallyo, branch `ui-v2` off `master`)

**Delete:** `src/lib/espn/**`, `src/lib/service/**`, `src/types/{game,team,stat,scoringPlay,odds,standings,GameContext,GameStatusEnums}.ts` ambient types, `OddsDashboard.tsx`, `LeagueOdds.tsx`, `src/app/api/stats/route.ts`.

**Keep verbatim:** `src/proxy.ts`, `next.config.ts` (espncdn.com images allowlist), `globals.css`/fonts, eslint/prettier/tsconfig, `scripts/generate-api-types.rb`, `src/app/maintenance/page.tsx`.

**Create (all typed off `api.generated.ts`):**
- `src/types/api-contract.ts` — aliases: `Game`, `Team`, `TeamStats`, `LeagueMetadata`, `CurrentContext`, `ApiError`, `GameDetails`, `StatLeader`, `ScoringPlay`, `StandingsGroup`, `StandingsTeam`.
- `src/lib/api/fetcher.ts` — carry as-is; `src/lib/api/client.ts` — typed URL builders: `gamesUrl({league, year, seasonType, week, date, timezone})`, `currentGamesUrl`, `contextUrl(league, mode, timezone)`, `leaguesUrl()`, `standingsUrl(league)`, `gameDetailsUrl(gameId)`.
- `src/app/api/_lib/backendProxy.ts` — single helper: build `${BACKEND_URL}` URL, inject `x-api-key`, map `timezone→userTimeZone`, transparent status/body/content-type error passthrough. Routes: `api/games/route.ts` (unwrap `.content`), `api/games/current/route.ts`, `api/context/route.ts` (mode `season→/games/context`, `date→/games/dates`), `api/leagues/route.ts`, `api/standings/route.ts` (**now proxies backend**), `api/games/[gameId]/details/route.ts`.
- `src/lib/gameStatus.ts` (identical logic incl. 6h `isLiveDashboardGame` window, typed `Game`), `src/lib/gameLayout.ts` (`getGameSides`, home-left MLS), `src/lib/leagues/leagueConfig.ts` (**drop** the `["nhl","mls"]` supportsStandings client override — backend flag is now authoritative; keep UI_PRESETS + `statsToDisplay` per `statsProfile`), `src/lib/leagues/statDisplayMaps.ts` (14 football / 12 hockey / 9 soccer keys, unchanged).
- Pages/components: `app/layout.tsx`, `app/page.tsx` (Dashboard, 10s poll, `isLiveDashboardGame` filter), `app/[league]/page.tsx` (SportPage: season/week/year selectors for season-mode, date selector for date-mode), `components/{Header,Footer,Dashboard,SportPage,Selector,League,CollapsableSection}.tsx`, `components/GameCard/{GameCard,CompactGameCard,FullSizeGameCard}.tsx`, `components/TeamCard/*`, `components/hooks/useLeagueState.ts`.
- `components/Standings.tsx` — carry the column-profile design (NFL/NHL/MLS/default profiles, section sorting, NHL division grouping + Div1-3/WC1-2 tagging) but read `team.stats["points"]` etc. via a tiny `stat(team, key)` helper against the typed `StandingsTeam`; identity fields (`seed`, `division`, `record`, `differential`) come typed.
- GameCard details: SWR on `/api/games/{id}/details`, `refreshInterval: 10000` while `shouldPollGameStats(status)`, single fetch when expanded-and-final; leaders keyed `${name}-${teamId}` client-side; team stats rendered from `game.stats.homeStats/awayStats` via the profile display map; spreadText for `supportsOdds` leagues.

## Phase 6 — Sequencing

1. Backend Phases 1–3 on `feature/ui-v2-api` (local only; **never push to main mid-work** — auto-deploy).
2. Phase 4 openapi on the same branch; regenerate types into `ui-v2`.
3. Phase 5 UI against `localhost:8080`.
4. Cutover: merge backend branch → main (deploys api.tallyo.us; old UI unaffected — all changes additive/compatible), smoke-test prod endpoints, then merge `ui-v2` → `master` (Vercel deploy).
5. Optional backfill: `POST /api/v1/games?league=X&year=Y&shouldFetchStats=true` per league to populate leaders/scoring plays for historical games.

## Phase 7 — End-to-end verification

Backend (local postgres + `API_KEY`, `./mvnw spring-boot:run`):

- Wait for a live game window (or POST backfill), then `/api/v1/games/{id}/details` for a live NFL game (leaders + plays present), a final game (still present after restart — proves persistence), and an unknown id → 404 envelope.

NHL wildcard tags and column sorting; `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAINTENANCE_MODE=true` redirect.
- `npm run lint && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build && npm run check:api-contract`.

## Open questions (genuinely unresolved)

1. **site.api.espn.com summary shape for NHL/MLS** — football has top-level `leaders`/`scoringPlays`; hockey/soccer may differ (soccer often uses `keyEvents`). Must curl-verify in Phase 3; the JsonNode mapper + per-sport branches are the mitigation, worst case MLS ships with empty leaders initially.
2. **Historical details gap** — pre-change final games have no persisted leaders/plays; decide whether to run the per-year backfill or accept empty details for old games.

### Critical Files for Implementation
- /Users/jackpotter/projects/tallyo-backend/src/main/java/com/tallyo/tallyo_backend/service/EspnService.java
- /Users/jackpotter/projects/tallyo-backend/src/main/java/com/tallyo/tallyo_backend/enums/League.java
- /Users/jackpotter/projects/tallyo-backend/openapi.yaml

- /Users/jackpotter/projects/tallyo/src/lib/leagues/leagueConfig.ts

# Tallyo UI Rebuild — Backend-Only Frontend + Backend API Additions

## Context

The current UI was built first, with logic later shifted into the Spring backend — leaving it split across two data planes: games/context/leagues come from the backend, but standings and per-game stats/scoring-plays are fetched directly from ESPN inside the frontend (`src/lib/espn` with its own mappers and hand-written ambient global types that diverge from the generated OpenAPI contract). This has made the UI hard to maintain.

**Goal:** rebuild the UI from scratch on a new branch as a *pure typed client* of the backend, and add the missing backend endpoints (standings, game details) so ESPN logic lives in exactly one place. Decisions confirmed with user: backend-only data flow, Next.js App Router again, full feature parity.

**Branches:** `ui-v2` in `tallyo` (off `master`), `feature/ui-v2-api` in `tallyo-backend` (off `main` — **never push to main mid-work**, it auto-deploys). All backend changes are additive/contract-compatible so the old UI keeps working until cutover.

---

## Phase 1 — Backend hardening (tallyo-backend, `feature/ui-v2-api`)

- `config/RestTemplateConfig.java` — add connect (5s) / read (10s) timeouts via `RestTemplateBuilder`. Required before adding standings fan-out; today a hung ESPN call can block the 20s scheduler thread forever.
- `enums/League.java` — flip `supportsStandings=true` and `supportsLiveDetails=true` for NHL and MLS (backend will now serve standings; frontend's client-side force-enable hack goes away).
- `config/CacheConfig.java` — add a `standings` cache to the `ConcurrentMapCacheManager` + a 30-min `@Scheduled` `@CacheEvict` for it.

## Phase 2 — Backend standings (greenfield, cache-only, no DB)

- **New** `config/EspnStandingsProperties.java` (`espn.standings.urls`: league id → ordered fallback URL list in `application.yml`) — copy the exact URLs from frontend `src/lib/espn/enums/espnEndpoints.ts` (nfl/cfb: single `cdn.espn.com/core/{league}/standings?xhr=1`; nhl: 7-URL fallback chain; mls: 2-URL chain).
- **New** `mapper/EspnStandingsMapper.java` — Jackson `JsonNode` port of `tallyo/src/lib/espn/mappers/standingsMapper.ts`: walk `content.standings.groups` / `children` / recursive `groups|children|items` → entries; per team: id/name/abbreviation/logo/location/seed + dynamic `stats[]` `type → displayValue` map; synthesize `record` and `differential`; sort by seed.
- **New** `service/StandingsServiceImpl` — `@Cacheable("standings", key = league)`; try fallback URLs until non-empty; all-fail → existing 502 path; `!league.isSupportsStandings()` → `InvalidRequestException` (400).
- **New** `controller/StandingsController.java` — `GET /api/v1/standings?league=` → `List<StandingsGroupResponse>`.
- **New DTOs:** `StandingsGroup { groupName, teams[] }`, `StandingsTeam { id, name, abbreviation, logo, location, seed?, conference?, division?, record?, differential?, stats: Map<String,String> }`.

## Phase 3 — Backend leaders + scoring plays (extend existing summary fetch — zero extra ESPN calls)

- **New entities** (created by `ddl-auto: update`; no league column → no `LeagueConstraintSync` change):
  - `ScoringPlay` / `ScoringPlayKey` — table `scoring_plays`, key `(gameId, playId)`; teamId, teamAbbreviation, displayText, homeScore, awayScore, scoringType, period, clock, sequence.
  - `GameLeader` / `GameLeaderKey` — table `game_leaders`, key `(gameId, teamId, statName)` (mirrors `GameStatKey`); displayName, shortDisplayName, value (Double), displayValue, playerName, playerShortName.
- `model/espn/box_score/EspnBoxscoreResponse.java` — add `JsonNode leaders` and `JsonNode scoringPlays` fields (currently dropped by `ignoreUnknown`).
- **New** `mapper/EspnSummaryDetailsMapper.java` — per-sport lenient extraction matching frontend `statsMapper.ts` field-for-field (football: top-level `leaders`/`scoringPlays`; hockey/soccer branches with null-safe empty-list fallbacks). **Curl-verify the site.api.espn.com summary shape for NHL and MLS during this phase** — it differs from the cdn.espn.com xhr payloads the old frontend scraped.
- `service/EspnService.java` (`attachStatsToGame`/`fetchStatsForGame`) — parse the one summary response into GameStats + GameLeaders + ScoringPlays; `entity/Game.java` gets two new cascaded `@OneToMany` collections + `addLeaders`/`addScoringPlays` helpers. The existing 20s live job then keeps details fresh automatically.
- **New endpoint** `GET /api/v1/games/{gameId}/details` in `GameController` (game id = ESPN event id, already the sole int PK — verified) → `GameDetails { gameId, leaders: StatLeader[], scoringPlays: ScoringPlay[] }`; unknown id → 404 `GAME_NOT_FOUND` (new `ResourceNotFoundException` in `GlobalExceptionHandler`).
  - `StatLeader { name, displayName, shortDisplayName, value?, displayValue, playerName, playerShortName, teamId }`
  - `ScoringPlay { id, teamId, teamName, displayText, homeScore, awayScore, scoringType, period, clock }`

## Phase 4 — Contract reconciliation (`openapi.yaml` → regenerate types)

Bump to 1.2.0, additions only:
- New paths: `/api/v1/standings`, `/api/v1/games/{gameId}/details`; document existing-but-missing `POST /api/v1/games` and deprecated `/games/nhl-dates`; add missing `size`/`page`/`sortBy` params.
- New schemas: `StandingsGroup`, `StandingsTeam` (dynamic `stats` via `additionalProperties: string`), `GameDetails`, `StatLeader`, `ScoringPlay`, `UpdateResponse`.
- Fix `Team` schema drift (add the ~14 real optional fields: seed, ranking, wins, losses, conference, division, records, pointsFor/Against, streak, etc.).
- In `tallyo` on `ui-v2`: `npm run gen:api-types`, commit regenerated `src/types/api.generated.ts`.

## Phase 5 — Frontend rebuild (tallyo, `ui-v2`)

**Delete:** `src/lib/espn/**`, `src/lib/service/**`, all ambient global types (`src/types/{game,team,stat,scoringPlay,odds,standings,GameContext,GameStatusEnums}.ts`), `OddsDashboard.tsx`, `LeagueOdds.tsx`, `src/app/api/stats/route.ts`.

**Keep verbatim:** `src/proxy.ts` (maintenance middleware), `next.config.ts` (espncdn images), `globals.css` + Geist fonts + prefers-color-scheme dark mode, eslint/prettier/tsconfig, `scripts/generate-api-types.rb`, `app/maintenance/page.tsx`.

**Create fresh (everything typed from `api.generated.ts` — no ambient globals):**
- `src/types/api-contract.ts` — aliases incl. new `GameDetails`, `StatLeader`, `ScoringPlay`, `StandingsGroup`, `StandingsTeam`.
- `src/app/api/_lib/backendProxy.ts` — single proxy helper: `${BACKEND_URL}` + `x-api-key`, `timezone→userTimeZone` mapping, transparent error passthrough. Routes: `games` (unwrap `.content`), `games/current`, `context` (mode season→`/games/context`, date→`/games/dates`), `leagues`, `standings` (**now proxies backend, not ESPN**), `games/[gameId]/details`.
- `src/lib/api/fetcher.ts` (carry ApiError-aware SWR fetcher) + `src/lib/api/client.ts` (typed URL builders per endpoint — no ad-hoc URL strings in components).
- `src/lib/gameStatus.ts` (same helpers incl. `isLiveDashboardGame` 6h window, `shouldPollGameStats`), `src/lib/gameLayout.ts` (`getGameSides`, MLS home-left), `src/lib/leagues/leagueConfig.ts` (**drop** the nhl/mls supportsStandings client override — backend flag now authoritative; keep UI_PRESETS for nfl/cfb season/week/year options), `src/lib/leagues/statDisplayMaps.ts` (presentation maps stay client-side, keyed by backend `statsProfile`).
- Pages/components: `layout.tsx`, `page.tsx` (Dashboard: live games per league, 10s poll), `[league]/page.tsx` → `SportPage` (context fetch, season/week/year or date selectors, games grid, standings), `Header`, `Footer`, `Selector`, `League`, `CollapsableSection`, `GameCard/{GameCard,CompactGameCard,FullSizeGameCard}`, `TeamCard/*` (possession arrow, NFL timeouts, winner styling), `Standings.tsx` (NFL/NHL/MLS/default column profiles, NHL division grouping + Div1-3/WC1-2 wildcard tagging, column sorting — reading typed `StandingsTeam` + `stats` map via a small helper).
- GameCard details: SWR `/api/games/{id}/details`, 10s refresh while `shouldPollGameStats`; team stats from `game.stats.homeStats/awayStats` via profile display map; `spreadText` odds for supportsOdds leagues.

## Phase 6 — Sequencing & cutover

1. Backend Phases 1–3 locally on the branch (postgres + `API_KEY`, `./mvnw spring-boot:run`).
2. Phase 4 contract, regenerate frontend types.
3. Phase 5 UI against `BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:8080`.
4. Cutover (user-driven, later): merge backend branch → main (deploys; old UI unaffected), smoke-test prod, then merge `ui-v2` → master (Vercel).
5. Optional: `POST /api/v1/games?league=X&year=Y&shouldFetchStats=true` backfill so historical finals get leaders/scoring plays (otherwise old games show empty details — acceptable).

## Verification

Backend: `./mvnw -q -DskipTests compile`; run locally; curl `/api/v1/standings` for all 4 leagues (NHL teams carry `division`, CFB has multiple groups; bogus league → 400 envelope); `/api/v1/games/{id}/details` for a live game (leaders + plays), after restart (persistence), unknown id (404); curl raw ESPN summary for one NHL + one MLS event to confirm mapper branches.

Frontend: `npm run lint && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build && npm run check:api-contract`; run dev against local backend and exercise: Dashboard live poll, NFL week/season/year selectors, NHL/MLS date selector, expanded cards (possession, timeouts, down/distance, last play, win probability, scoring plays, leaders, team stats, spreadText, ESPN link, venue), standings all 4 leagues, maintenance-mode redirect.

## Known risks / open items

- **ESPN summary shape for NHL/MLS** on site.api.espn.com may differ from football (soccer often uses `keyEvents`) — verified by curl in Phase 3; JsonNode mapper branches are the mitigation.
- Standings payloads from cdn.espn.com are large and loosely shaped — the lenient JsonNode port mirrors the battle-tested frontend mapper rather than strict POJOs, deliberately.

- **New DTOs:** `StandingsGroup { groupName, teams[] }`, `StandingsTeam { id, name, abbreviation, logo, location, seed?, conference?, division?, record?, differential?, stats: Map<String,String> }`.

## Phase 3 — Backend leaders + scoring plays (extend existing summary fetch — zero extra ESPN calls)

- **New entities** (created by `ddl-auto: update`; no league column → no `LeagueConstraintSync` change):
  - `ScoringPlay` / `ScoringPlayKey` — table `scoring_plays`, key `(gameId, playId)`; teamId, teamAbbreviation, displayText, homeScore, awayScore, scoringType, period, clock, sequence.
  - `GameLeader` / `GameLeaderKey` — table `game_leaders`, key `(gameId, teamId, statName)` (mirrors `GameStatKey`); displayName, shortDisplayName, value (Double), displayValue, playerName, playerShortName.
- `model/espn/box_score/EspnBoxscoreResponse.java` — add `JsonNode leaders` and `JsonNode scoringPlays` fields (currently dropped by `ignoreUnknown`).
- **New** `mapper/EspnSummaryDetailsMapper.java` — per-sport lenient extraction matching frontend `statsMapper.ts` field-for-field (football: top-level `leaders`/`scoringPlays`; hockey/soccer branches with null-safe empty-list fallbacks). **Curl-verify the site.api.espn.com summary shape for NHL and MLS during this phase** — it differs from the cdn.espn.com xhr payloads the old frontend scraped.
- `service/EspnService.java` (`attachStatsToGame`/`fetchStatsForGame`) — parse the one summary response into GameStats + GameLeaders + ScoringPlays; `entity/Game.java` gets two new cascaded `@OneToMany` collections + `addLeaders`/`addScoringPlays` helpers. The existing 20s live job then keeps details fresh automatically.
- **New endpoint** `GET /api/v1/games/{gameId}/details` in `GameController` (game id = ESPN event id, already the sole int PK — verified) → `GameDetails { gameId, leaders: StatLeader[], scoringPlays: ScoringPlay[] }`; unknown id → 404 `GAME_NOT_FOUND` (new `ResourceNotFoundException` in `GlobalExceptionHandler`).
  - `StatLeader { name, displayName, shortDisplayName, value?, displayValue, playerName, playerShortName, teamId }`
  - `ScoringPlay { id, teamId, teamName, displayText, homeScore, awayScore, scoringType, period, clock }`

## Phase 4 — Contract reconciliation (`openapi.yaml` → regenerate types)

Bump to 1.2.0, additions only:
- New paths: `/api/v1/standings`, `/api/v1/games/{gameId}/details`; document existing-but-missing `POST /api/v1/games` and deprecated `/games/nhl-dates`; add missing `size`/`page`/`sortBy` params.
- New schemas: `StandingsGroup`, `StandingsTeam` (dynamic `stats` via `additionalProperties: string`), `GameDetails`, `StatLeader`, `ScoringPlay`, `UpdateResponse`.
- Fix `Team` schema drift (add the ~14 real optional fields: seed, ranking, wins, losses, conference, division, records, pointsFor/Against, streak, etc.).
- In `tallyo` on `ui-v2`: `npm run gen:api-types`, commit regenerated `src/types/api.generated.ts`.

## Phase 5 — Frontend rebuild (tallyo, `ui-v2`)

**Delete:** `src/lib/espn/**`, `src/lib/service/**`, all ambient global types (`src/types/{game,team,stat,scoringPlay,odds,standings,GameContext,GameStatusEnums}.ts`), `OddsDashboard.tsx`, `LeagueOdds.tsx`, `src/app/api/stats/route.ts`.

**Keep verbatim:** `src/proxy.ts` (maintenance middleware), `next.config.ts` (espncdn images), `globals.css` + Geist fonts + prefers-color-scheme dark mode, eslint/prettier/tsconfig, `scripts/generate-api-types.rb`, `app/maintenance/page.tsx`.

**Create fresh (everything typed from `api.generated.ts` — no ambient globals):**
- `src/types/api-contract.ts` — aliases incl. new `GameDetails`, `StatLeader`, `ScoringPlay`, `StandingsGroup`, `StandingsTeam`.
- `src/app/api/_lib/backendProxy.ts` — single proxy helper: `${BACKEND_URL}` + `x-api-key`, `timezone→userTimeZone` mapping, transparent error passthrough. Routes: `games` (unwrap `.content`), `games/current`, `context` (mode season→`/games/context`, date→`/games/dates`), `leagues`, `standings` (**now proxies backend, not ESPN**), `games/[gameId]/details`.
- `src/lib/api/fetcher.ts` (carry ApiError-aware SWR fetcher) + `src/lib/api/client.ts` (typed URL builders per endpoint — no ad-hoc URL strings in components).
- `src/lib/gameStatus.ts` (same helpers incl. `isLiveDashboardGame` 6h window, `shouldPollGameStats`), `src/lib/gameLayout.ts` (`getGameSides`, MLS home-left), `src/lib/leagues/leagueConfig.ts` (**drop** the nhl/mls supportsStandings client override — backend flag now authoritative; keep UI_PRESETS for nfl/cfb season/week/year options), `src/lib/leagues/statDisplayMaps.ts` (presentation maps stay client-side, keyed by backend `statsProfile`).
- Pages/components: `layout.tsx`, `page.tsx` (Dashboard: live games per league, 10s poll), `[league]/page.tsx` → `SportPage` (context fetch, season/week/year or date selectors, games grid, standings), `Header`, `Footer`, `Selector`, `League`, `CollapsableSection`, `GameCard/{GameCard,CompactGameCard,FullSizeGameCard}`, `TeamCard/*` (possession arrow, NFL timeouts, winner styling), `Standings.tsx` (NFL/NHL/MLS/default column profiles, NHL division grouping + Div1-3/WC1-2 wildcard tagging, column sorting — reading typed `StandingsTeam` + `stats` map via a small helper).
- GameCard details: SWR `/api/games/{id}/details`, 10s refresh while `shouldPollGameStats`; team stats from `game.stats.homeStats/awayStats` via profile display map; `spreadText` odds for supportsOdds leagues.

## Phase 6 — Sequencing & cutover

1. Backend Phases 1–3 locally on the branch (postgres + `API_KEY`, `./mvnw spring-boot:run`).
2. Phase 4 contract, regenerate frontend types.
3. Phase 5 UI against `BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:8080`.
4. Cutover (user-driven, later): merge backend branch → main (deploys; old UI unaffected), smoke-test prod, then merge `ui-v2` → master (Vercel).
5. Optional: `POST /api/v1/games?league=X&year=Y&shouldFetchStats=true` backfill so historical finals get leaders/scoring plays (otherwise old games show empty details — acceptable).

## Verification

Backend: `./mvnw -q -DskipTests compile`; run locally; curl `/api/v1/standings` for all 4 leagues (NHL teams carry `division`, CFB has multiple groups; bogus league → 400 envelope); `/api/v1/games/{id}/details` for a live game (leaders + plays), after restart (persistence), unknown id (404); curl raw ESPN summary for one NHL + one MLS event to confirm mapper branches.

Frontend: `npm run lint && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build && npm run check:api-contract`; run dev against local backend and exercise: Dashboard live poll, NFL week/season/year selectors, NHL/MLS date selector, expanded cards (possession, timeouts, down/distance, last play, win probability, scoring plays, leaders, team stats, spreadText, ESPN link, venue), standings all 4 leagues, maintenance-mode redirect.

## Known risks / open items

- **ESPN summary shape for NHL/MLS** on site.api.espn.com may differ from football (soccer often uses `keyEvents`) — verified by curl in Phase 3; JsonNode mapper branches are the mitigation.
- Standings payloads from cdn.espn.com are large and loosely shaped — the lenient JsonNode port mirrors the battle-tested frontend mapper rather than strict POJOs, deliberately.
